name: context-aware-triage
description: Retrieval-augmented triage — context engineering in miniature. A retriever first pulls the known issues most similar to the incoming report and frames a triage packet; judge-triage then classifies WITH that retrieved context in view, so the duplicate branch actually works (a triage judge can't call something a duplicate it was never shown). The fix for the dedup gap: give the judge the right context, not all the context.

inputs.name: knownIssues
inputs.description: Corpus of existing/known issues to dedup against. Paste a list, or wire it from a source (Jira search, an issues export). Empty = no corpus, every novel report reads as actionable.

phases.name: retrieve-related
phases.description: Scoped retrieval + framing: surface only the known issues similar to this report, and frame a packet the judge can act on. Combines retrieve+frame in one pass so the route's input carries both the report and its candidates.
phases.prompt:
Frame a triage packet for duplicate detection. Output TWO clearly-headed sections, verbatim:
first `=== INCOMING REPORT ===` with the report below it,
then `=== RELATED KNOWN ISSUES (retrieved) ===` with the entries from the corpus most similar to the report (or `none found`).

REPORT:
${input}

KNOWN ISSUES CORPUS:
${knownIssues}

phases.name: triage
phases.description: Classify with the retrieved context in view — duplicate detection now has something to match against.

actionable.name: open-ticket
actionable.description: Novel + real (no strong match in the retrieved issues) → file a ticket.

duplicate.name: link-duplicate
duplicate.description: Matches a retrieved known issue → link to it and acknowledge, no new ticket.

code.source: return 'Recorded as not-a-bug (noise/working-as-designed). No action taken.'

needs-info.name: ask-for-info
needs-info.description: Plausible but too vague — request repro steps and specifics.
